data.title: Norway’s Sovereign Wealth Fund to Again Oppose Elon Musk’s $1 Trillion Pay Package
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Norway’s $2.2 trillion sovereign wealth fund said it would vote against Elon Musk’s 2025 compensation package at Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting on December 3.

The world’s largest sovereign wealth fund said total compensation needs greater transparency and that “the board should ensure that all benefits have a clear business rationale.”

The vote this year is nonbinding. The package is widely considered the largest corporate executive compensation plan ever and could ultimately provide Musk with up to $1 trillion in stock compensation over the next decade.

data.title: CZ Says Security Is "Always the Most Important Thing" as Binance Blockchain Week Closes Day One in Bangkok
data.description: Changpeng Zhao (CZ), founder and former CEO of Binance, took the stage at Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok on Saturday for a wide-ranging fireside chat with The Block's Head of Multimedia, Gareth Jenkinson, under the banner "CZ: What Comes Next? A Fireside on Innovation, Investment and the Future of Finance." Coming just weeks after one of the most sophisticated security incidents in the crypto industry's history, CZ did not shy away from the toughest questions of the day. Over the course of roughly forty minutes, he unpacked the anatomy of the hack, called for a new era of industry-wide collaboration, weighed in on the Nvidia founder saga and government intervention in markets, discussed where YZi Labs is deploying capital across crypto, AI, and biotech, and offered a sober but ultimately optimistic read on the current bear market. Below are the key takeaways.On the Binance Hack: "It Can Be Completely Prevented"Asked for his assessment of the incident, CZ was direct: the exchange's team had grown complacent. "There's been many years without issues, and it's the most hacked target," he said. "The company's senior leaders were not focused enough on security. They were dealing with many other issues — many of them are very important, but security is always the most important thing."CZ described an attack that began with social engineering rather than code. Hackers targeted "1,000 or more" Binance employees — starting with non-technical staff — using real recruiters to lure them into fake job interviews, where a "Zoom upgrade" link delivered a Trojan horse. From there, the attackers moved laterally, mapping the organization to identify security engineers, DevOps staff, and production deployment teams.According to CZ, once inside, the attackers exfiltrated source code and used AI to analyze it at unprecedented speed. "The analysis that used to take a normal person six months is now done with the support of AI in a day." The attack was complex enough that hackers couldn't breach the hot wallet directly and instead exploited a weakness in Ethereum's EIP-7702 signing protocol.Looking back, CZ said the breach "can be completely prevented," but praised Binance's response. No users were left in the dark, there was little panic among VIP clients and partners, and the exchange covered user losses. "That continued from the ethos when I was founder — we've got to protect our users."He noted Binance drew down roughly half of its SAFU insurance fund (about $1 billion) and half of its Futures Insurance Fund. "From a risk management perspective, it's important that you have enough resources to cover the medium, severe, even the most severe instances."Calling for an Industry Security AllianceCZ used the moment to push for closer collaboration across the industry. He outlined a three-step vision for what he called an industry security alliance: instant response, sharing best security practices, and cross-checking each other's systems. He emphasized that in this incident, Binance received critical help from Circle, Tether, and U.S. intelligence agencies including the Secret Service and FBI to freeze funds.He also argued that "security by obscurity no longer works." Because hackers will almost certainly obtain a copy of a company's source code, CZ suggested firms may as well embrace greater transparency. "The hackers are using every other AI to scan your source code. They don't care about your privacy."The fight, he said, is inherently asymmetric. "To defend, you have to find every problem and fix it. To attack, you only need to find one problem." He pointed to a broader wave of attacks — "5-10 hacks every single day" reported, and likely more unreported — and urged teams to spend "30, 50, 80% of your time on security if needed for the next few months.""Let Binance be the alarm," he said. "Do not let that happen to you."On Nvidia, Founders, and Government InterventionTurning to the Nvidia saga, CZ reiterated his view that it was a mistake for the company to let Jensen Huang step away. "Without him, Nvidia will coast for a while, but there's a very high chance there will be issues. Nvidia right now has basically a monopoly on chip design, which is hugely beneficial for the U.S. and actually for the world."CZ described himself as "always pro-founder," noting that YZi Labs avoids the practice of pushing founders out of the companies it backs. "A company lives or dies with a founder in a lot of cases." Still, he acknowledged that every founder's goal should be to build a company that can continue to operate without them.On reports that President Trump phoned into Nvidia's board meeting, CZ was measured but aligned with the principle that governments should be cautious about interfering in private business. "When you have an external force interfering with markets, you're promoting the less competitive players and removing the market's ability to select the best companies and let the worst companies die." He was careful to note that the pressure on Huang may itself have been government-driven, and that he isn't deeply involved in U.S. politics.AI, Investment, and the Case for CryptoCZ confirmed he continues to lean heavily on AI, calling the newest generation of models "very, very powerful" and increasingly capable of controlling computers and writing software on his behalf. He revealed a specific interest in using AI for security scanning — particularly open-source models, which he finds have "much less guardrails" and can scan code more deeply for defensive purposes.On investing, CZ explained that YZi Labs focuses on three sectors: crypto, AI, and biotech. In Web3, the firm makes more early-stage bets through incubation programs and hackathons. In AI, tickets are larger and later-stage, reflecting his view that AI is "highly concentrated and highly centralized" — few players can access the tens or hundreds of thousands of chips required to compete at the frontier.Counterintuitively, he said now is a compelling time to invest in crypto. "A lot of hot money went to investing in AI. I still believe crypto is actually the best time to invest." He downplayed AI as a replacement for blockchain: "Blockchain doesn't replace the internet. AI does not replace the internet. AI also does not replace money — AI is going to need a lot more money and a lot more transactions. The technology for money is not going away."A Mature Bear Market and the Reality of CyclesAddressing an industry that he acknowledged feels "dejected and bearish," CZ framed the current downturn as comparatively mild. He noted Bitcoin's lows across past cycles — $150 in 2015, $3,100 in 2018, $16,000 in 2022 — and contrasted them with this cycle, where $60,000 is viewed as "really bad." He pointed to the previous all-time high as a sign of how far the market has matured."Markets only bottom when there's maximum fear. I think we're pretty close to that," he said, declining to make price predictions. He also observed that each cycle brings in more newcomers and more non-technical participants, changing the character of the community.His long-term framing was emphatic: in his adult life, there have been three defining technologies — the internet, blockchain, and AI — and they don't replace one another. He cited SpaceX and Starlink as proof that innovation can flourish even decades after a technology matures. "There's going to be a lot more innovations in the blockchain space. The blockchain industry is not going away. Humans, agents — they're all going to use money."On the challenge of educating policymakers, CZ was pragmatic. "Politicians are so busy. They can only spend five minutes on each topic. We cannot expect politicians to understand technology fully." His answer was persistent education: more conferences, more think tanks, more accessible material. "There are no shortcuts. You got to do your reading, you got to do your homework."

data.title: US Consumers Ease Spending After Third-Quarter Burst
data.description: US consumers eased spending last month after a burst in the third quarter helped deliver the strongest economic growth in three years, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Hyperliquid Labs Unstakes 60,000 Tokens, Plans December 6 Team Distribution
data.description: Hyperliquid Labs has unstaked 60,000 tokens. According to Odaily, it plans to distribute them to team members on December 6.

data.title: Polymarket’s Bitcoin November 28 $60,000 Yes Odds Fall 17.5 Percentage Points
data.description: The Yes probability for the $60,000 submarket in Polymarket’s “Bitcoin Breaks Through on November 28” event fell to 22.5%. According to ChainCatcher, the probability was 40% one hour earlier, a decline of 17.5 percentage points.

data.title: POSCO Union Votes to Accept Wage Agreement
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the union at South Korean steelmaker POSCO said its members voted on Saturday to accept the company's wage proposal after five months of negotiations. The approved terms include a 2.6% increase in base pay, a one-time payment of 6.2 million won (about $4,600), and improved employee benefits.

The union had initially sought a 7.1% base-pay increase, a performance bonus equal to 600% of base pay, 50 shares for each employee, and a holiday bonus equal to 200% of base pay. It also raised concerns about staff shortages and aging facilities, saying they could increase the risk of workplace accidents.

Management had previously offered a 2.5% base-pay increase and a one-time payment of 5 million won. After 31 rounds of negotiations since June, the two sides reached a tentative agreement on October 30 for a 2.6% base-pay increase and a one-time payment of 6 million won. Union members rejected that agreement on November 7 and sought better terms.

data.title: Binance Opens Four-Challenge Blockchain Week Treasure Hunt
data.description:
Binance announced on X that its #BinanceBlockchainWeek treasure hunt is open now. Participants must have a registered Binance account, complete KYC, finish four challenges to collect all four pins, and submit the survey.

The first 12 eligible hunters with complete, valid submissions will receive prizes: six tennis sets and six 9YA prizes. Winners can collect their prizes at the Swag Station on Day 2. Submissions close at 3 PM (UTC+7), Nov 29.

The promotion is unavailable to residents of the US, UK, EEA, Hong Kong, Singapore, and jurisdictions on Binance’s prohibited list.

data.title: Spanish Prime Minister Sánchez: We Also Oppose Spending 5% of GDP on Defense
data.description: According to Jin10, Spanish Prime Minister Sánchez said, “We also oppose allocating 5% of GDP to defense spending.”

data.title: Duan Yongping: Elon Musk Has Significantly Improved My Quality of Life
data.description:
Duan Yongping said on November 27 that Elon Musk had significantly improved his quality of life, citing his use of a Tesla and Starlink.

According to Odaily, he was responding to a social media user who said they had been an early Tesla customer and sold their Model S only this year. The user proposed a $2 bet: $1 that Tesla’s share price would be lower in 10 years than it is today, and $1 that Apple’s would be higher. Duan said he had neither won nor lost, but had “actually won” because he drives a Tesla and uses Starlink.

data.title: TRM Labs Executive Calls Recovery the Largest in Human History
data.description: Binance announced on X that Jonno Newman, Head of Deployment Strategy APAC at TRM Labs, described the event as both the biggest crypto hack and the biggest recovery in human history.

data.title: Arthur Hayes: December Fed Meeting to Be Key for Sentiment as Nasdaq and Tech Stocks May Stay Under Pressure
data.description:
Maelstrom Chief Investment Officer Arthur Hayes said the Federal Reserve’s December FOMC meeting would be important for market sentiment. According to Odaily, Hayes expects selling in the Nasdaq and technology stocks to resume, potentially weighing further on Bitcoin.

Hayes said he would look for gold to rise and the Nasdaq to fall. He described the failure of a U.S. bank last Friday as a minor market tremor.

On the possibility of further Fed rate increases, Hayes said he did not mind if markets experienced more pain, as he believes a bailout would eventually follow. He said the key question is how much pain markets must endure before policymakers resume monetary easing. These were his personal market views.

data.title: Chainflip Tracks Attacker and Develops User Fund Recovery Plan
data.description: Chainflip is tracking the attacker and developing a plan to recover user funds. According to Odaily, the team is pursuing on-chain and off-chain leads and designing a recovery fund to be managed through on-chain records and protocol governance. Unpaid loans will be settled at prices in effect when the attack occurred. The stolen BTC has not been moved, and ETH deposited in Tornado Cash may also remain unmoved. Chainflip has reported the incident to relevant law enforcement agencies and is offering a 10% bounty if the attacker returns 90% of the funds. The protocol remains paused and will not restart until its security review and remediation are complete.

data.title: Bank of England Urges Financial Firms to Accelerate Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration
data.description:
The Bank of England urged financial institutions to accelerate migration to post-quantum cryptography to address risks from quantum computing. According to Odaily, the central bank said in its November Financial Stability Report that quantum computing could threaten widely used public-key cryptography, affecting financial transactions, identity authentication and digital signatures. It urged firms to plan migrations early, identify cryptographic dependencies in existing systems and prioritize upgrades to critical operations.

Under the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre’s roadmap, financial institutions should develop migration plans by the end of 2028, complete migrations for high-priority operations by the end of 2031 and migrate other systems by the end of 2035. The Bank of England also said the financial system’s high degree of interconnection means delays by a single institution or third-party provider could amplify systemic risks.

data.title: Thailand Raids Suspected Crypto Exchange Operation in Pattaya With About 200 Million Baht in Monthly Transactions
data.description:
Thai police and Chonburi immigration officials raided a house and an apartment in Pattaya on November 27, arresting six Chinese nationals. According to Odaily, police suspect the group used a USDT exchange business as cover to handle about 200 million baht a month, with some funds possibly linked to scams and online gambling; the victims were mainly in China.

Five Chinese nationals were found conducting USDT exchanges at the house, where officers seized computers, 13 phones, a router and three cryptocurrency hardware wallets. At an apartment in Jomtien, officers arrested another Chinese man, He Yalong, whom investigators suspect of directing the group, and seized two desktop computers and two phones.

Police said the group may have moved illicit funds through transactions related to online shopping. Authorities have not announced specific charges. Chonburi immigration officials will continue tracing the funds and investigating other possible participants. The six detainees will be deported after Thai legal proceedings are completed.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Warns of AI Risks, Sees Crypto Bull Market After Crisis
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Block, Arthur Hayes discussed the risk of overinvestment in the AI industry and outlined three concerns. Debt spreads for AI hyperscalers are widening, with some nearing levels associated with default risk; he singled out Oracle’s credit default swaps for attention.

Hayes said U.S. President Donald Trump’s involvement in decisions related to Nvidia suggests the U.S. government recognizes the need to rescue the company. He added that monetary authorities would also need to support the response.

Hayes said an “incredible cryptocurrency bull market” could begin after the process is over.

data.title: Binance CMO Eowyn Chen Invites Security Leaders to Discuss AI-Era Threats
data.description: Binance announced on X that Binance CMO Eowyn Chen invited security leaders from Binance, Elliptic, Mandiant, Microsoft and AWS to discuss evolving cyber threats, how organizations can strengthen defenses and the importance of cross-industry collaboration at Binance Blockchain Week today. The discussion addressed cybersecurity challenges amid the development of AI.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Leopold Aschenbrenner's Q3 Letter Bets on AI Agents and Superintelligence, Names 10 Potential Beneficiaries
data.description:
Situational Awareness founder Leopold Aschenbrenner said in his third-quarter investor letter that markets are underestimating how quickly AI will advance from chatbots to agents and superintelligence. He projected that 2027 could bring AI advances on a scale equivalent to those of the previous three years.

According to Odaily, Aschenbrenner’s investment focus spans five areas: foundation models, memory chips, GPU rentals, data-center power supply and robotics. He named Anthropic, SK Hynix, Kioxia, SanDisk, SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, IREN and Bloom Energy as 10 companies to watch.

Aschenbrenner also said some software companies, AI-wrapper businesses, chip designers and current AI industry winners could lose competitive advantages as AI gradually replaces engineers, code, intellectual property and management capabilities. He listed Salesforce, Adobe, ServiceNow, C3.ai, Synopsys, Arm, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and ASML as companies to approach cautiously. The views are his own and are not definitive market forecasts.

data.title: XRP Holders Seek 31.1 Billion Escrow Burn; David Schwartz Says Validators Cannot Force Ripple
data.description:
Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said XRP Ledger validators cannot force Ripple to burn its escrowed XRP, even with more than 80% support. A group called Make XRP Great Again urged Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse in an open letter on November 16 to burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027, according to BeInCrypto.

An amendment requires 29 of 35 validator votes and must maintain that support for two weeks before activation. Schwartz said a majority can change its own rules but cannot compel dissenting validators or seize Ripple’s escrow; validators backing a burn amendment would instead isolate themselves from the network. He said in February 2024 that Ripple could mimic a burn by sending escrow releases to an account no one controls. Ripple reported about 31.1 billion XRP and plans to release 1 billion XRP from escrow on December 1. XRP traded near $0.95, down nearly 30% in a month.

data.title: India’s Central Bank Intensifies Scrutiny of $247 Billion Gold-Loan Sector as Prices Fall
data.description:
According to Jin10, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is intensifying scrutiny of the country’s $247 billion gold-loan industry as falling gold prices erode the collateral value lenders require from borrowers. RBI officials have reviewed early indicators of stress, asset quality, and loan amounts relative to pledged gold. Banks and shadow lenders can lend up to 85% of gold’s value, and the RBI has conducted preventive inspections for breaches of that limit, but has found no evidence of violations so far.

Shadow lenders saw signs of borrower stress in the quarter ended September. A revised rule prohibiting interest-payment deferrals also led to higher default rates. Gold prices have fallen 30% since peaking in January, with the decline accelerating in recent weeks amid expectations that the Federal Reserve will take a more hawkish stance.

data.title: Binance Blockchain Week: Industry Leaders Call for "Collective Resilience" as AI Reshapes Crypto Security
data.description:
Security took center stage at Binance Blockchain Week 2026 as industry leaders convened for a panel titled "Collective Resilience: Securing the Digital Asset Industry in the AI Era."
The session brought together Jimmy Su, Chief Security Officer at Binance; Vivek Chudgar, Managing Director JAPAC at Mandiant Consulting, Google; Silvia Ihensekhien, Chief Security Advisor, GCR at Microsoft; and Pooja Saha, Sr. Security & Compliance BD Manager of APJC at AWS. Eowyn Chen, Binance's Chief Marketing Officer, moderated the discussion.
Jimmy Su noted that AI is "changing the economics and the speed of cyber attacks," enabling attackers to bridge knowledge gaps and compress attack timeframes — a particular challenge for crypto's 24/7, largely irreversible transactions.
Guests also discussed AI-enabled tactics — deepfakes, AI-written malware, automated reconnaissance, and LLM-based phishing at scale — citing North Korean groups using AI-generated deepfake video calls to steal over $400 million in crypto over 18 months.
Panelists agreed that while AI changes the scale and speed of attacks, cybersecurity fundamentals remain unchanged. Vivek Chudgar stressed visibility ("if you can't see, you can't stop"), understanding weak signals, and rapid response, urging startups to tightly manage privileged access, avoid architectural "built-in trust," and build telemetry.
Pooja Saha emphasized AWS's shared responsibility model, urging builders to define clear ownership and boundaries for AI agents.
Guests also discussed cross-industry information sharing, noting crypto lacks the coordinated threat intelligence seen in banking and healthcare. Standardization and pre-built trust protocols were flagged as critical.
Jimmy Su outlined Binance's three-pronged transformation: asset-centric security, containment to limit blast radius, and rapid response. He called for a shift "from individual security to collective resilience," envisioning collective intelligence where a hack detected by one company reaches collaborators within seconds.
Chen summarized the takeaway: design with zero trust, but "for our industry to move forward, we need to build a trust protocol."
